cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt, friends. Jeroboam returned from Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon (2 Chronicles 10:2). Solomon, David's son (1 Kings 2:12) and Israel's king, was the one he ran from. A man who ran that far doesn't come back for nothing, and I think people were about to notice.

The answer is to lighten the burden his father put on them, friends. They said, “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you must lighten the burden of your father’s service…” (2 Chronicles 10:4). A yoke is the wooden beam an ox wears to pull a load, so they're talking about heavy work. And they made a promise too: “…and we will serve you.” That's a pretty fair deal.

The answer is False, friends. The people said, “…you must lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.” (2 Chronicles 10:4). They ask for lighter work and promise to serve him if he does it. That's not a threat. It's a deal waiting for a yes.

The answer is the elders who had served Solomon, friends. Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime (2 Chronicles 10:6). Solomon was David's son (1 Kings 2:12) and Israel's king before him. These men had watched the old king work up close. I'd say that's a good first phone call.

The answer is kind, friends. The elders said, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.” (2 Chronicles 10:7). Notice they say kind twice. When advice repeats a word, I'd write that word on my apron.

The answer is True, friends. The elders said, “If you will be kind to these people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.” (2 Chronicles 10:7). That's a big promise from some seasoned advisors. Kind words on one side, servants forever on the other.

The answer is the young men who grew up with him, friends. Rehoboam rejected the elders' advice and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him (2 Chronicles 10:8). They'd known him for years. I bet that group felt a lot more comfortable than the elders.

The answer is that he will add to it, friends. The young men said to tell them, “Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke.” (2 Chronicles 10:11). The people asked for a lighter load and the advice was a heavier one. That's the opposite of what they wanted, and it's not even close.

The answer is God, friends. The text says, “So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from God…” (2 Chronicles 10:15). So there's more going on here than a king who wouldn't listen. That's worth sitting with for a moment.

The answer is Jeroboam son of Nebat, friends. The text says this was “…in order that the LORD might fulfill the word that He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.” (2 Chronicles 10:15). Ahijah's word came to the very man standing in that crowd. Jeroboam was the one it was spoken to.

The answer is that they turned from David's house and went home, friends. They said, “To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” and “…all the Israelites went home…” (2 Chronicles 10:16). They said it and then they walked. The conversation was over.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “…but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.” (2 Chronicles 10:17). The Israelites went home, but the ones in Judah's cities still had him as king. He was still reigning.

The answer is that he flees in his chariot to Jerusalem, friends. The text says, “And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.” (2 Chronicles 10:18). In haste, no speeches. A few days ago this man was giving the people a harsh answer, and now he's leaving fast.
